subject: SLA health debrief + OKR implications from 2027-05-01 GPU cluster incident
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA health debrief + OKR implications from 2027-05-01 GPU cluster incident

Team —

Quick debrief attached from the cluster incident that impacted hosted inference in us-west for ~46 minutes on 2027-05-01. This note focuses on executive-facing points for the QBR and the direct implications for our SLO/OKR runway. Highlights: 

- Root cause (short): kernel regression in the driver rollout that led to memory fragmentation on 8xA100 pools, triggering degraded scheduling and automatic capacity shedding.
- SLA impact: 46 minutes of partial-degradation window, affecting 18 accounts at p99 latency > SLA threshold; estimated token-weighted SLA slip = 0.14% for the region.
- Customer escalations: EnterpriseExample submitted an ops ticket and requested a post-incident call. They saw intermittent timeouts on their batch scoring jobs.
- Immediate mitigations executed: emergency rollback to previous driver, manual cache flush on affected nodes, scaled up warm spare pool to reduce scheduling pressure.

Attached: timeline, raw SLA calc, and an OKR implication one-pager that maps this to our Reliability OKR (R-1.1: reduce region-wide p99 latency regressions).

Asks: 
1) Vivek — want a one-slide executive summary for the QBR that calls out customer impact, root cause, remediation, and 3 proposed control changes.
2) Marissa — please confirm proposed owners for the action items in the attached spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.
3) Marcus — we need a short note on longer-term kernel validation guardrails (test coverage + canary policy) for the postmortem.

Ive included external ops contacts at EnterpriseExample and our cloud partner for traceability. Ill host a 30-min readout for leadership tomorrow at 10:00 if that works — calendar invite to follow.

Attachments: [Attachment: gpu-cluster-incident-timeline.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)], [Attachment: sla-impact-calculation.xlsx (XLSX, 240KB)], [Attachment: okr-impact-one-pager.docx (DOCX, 95KB)]

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Director, Reliability Programs
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jasmine — good concise framing. Two quick asks from me: 

1) For the QBR slide, keep the executive narrative to one bullet about customer impact (EnterpriseExample) and one line on financial exposure (estimate in the calc). Dont overload with technical detail — point them to the appendix.
2) Prioritize two controls for immediate motion: (a) driver rollout canary policy (auto-block on memory regressions) and (b) SLA-weighted on-call paging to include token-weighted alerts.

Ill attend the readout tomorrow. Please add a short "customer outreach" status row in the spreadsheet — who talked to the customer and what did we promise (credits, timeline).

-Vivek

Thanks — quick technical note for the postmortem appendix and the QBR appendix: 

- Immediate RC validation: weve reproduced the memory fragmentation locally in a staging canary with the same driver build; root cause confirmed.
- Short-term control: I propose a two-stage canary: (1) functional smoke + memory/regression probe for new drivers in a canary pool; (2) automated rollback trigger if memory fragmentation metric exceeds threshold X for >5m. Ill draft the exact metric definition and add to the spreadsheet.
- Long-term: expand job-level graceful degradation to reduce token-weighted impact during scheduling pressure (approx 6-8 week work).

Ive attached an initial test plan snippet in the shared drive link. Also — do we want to include a recommended SLA credit band for affected customers? Laura, can you confirm what we promised verbally on the call?

-Marcus
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
